meaning: Stable unique identifier, prefixed by facet (CRK, CDI, SYS, INT, OUT, OTC, IMP, ADP, TRT, STK, CCC). Retired IDs are never reused.
The single fundamental aspect the term belongs to. Values and definitions in master_v5_controlled_values.csv.
Depth of the term within its facet hierarchy. Computed from Parent ID - never edit by hand.
The broader term one level up (a true is-a parent). Blank for a top-level (L1) term.
The atomic concept name, sentence case, one concept per entry. Leading spaces encode hierarchy depth (derived - never edit by hand).
Genus-differentia definition: opens with the parent's term (or the facet notion at L1), 1-2 sentences, neutral wording, general definition only - contextual climate material lives in CGIAR example.
The named authority the definition draws on, hierarchy IPCC > AGROVOC > FAO/WMO/UNFCCC; glossary-cited definitions keep the source's defining sentence essentially verbatim.
The term's position in the results-chain view.
Whether the term serves adaptation, mitigation, or both.
How the term relates to adaptation: specific (always counts), conditional (counts only under the stated condition), or n/a.
The condition under which the term counts as adaptation.
How the term relates to mitigation.
The condition under which the term counts as mitigation.
The topical subject area, kept out of the hierarchy; every term has exactly one.
The single CGIAR Impact Area the term serves, or Cross-cutting.
Associative (non-hierarchical) links to other terms, each with a relation label, e.g. 'part-of: INT_319; produces: OUT_062'.
The origin taxonomy or combination the term came from (e.g. 'New (v5)').
The original identifiers from the source files, left untouched.
The verbatim pre-revision label, where the term was renamed.
A concrete CGIAR example illustrating the term, and/or the contextual climate interpretation ('Climate context: ...') moved out of the definition under the two-part structure.
Alternative labels for the same concept - same meaning in both directions; one word belongs to one term.
A supporting link for the example or definition.
